_meta.purpose: Concrete model and effort recommendations per AI tool, for each difficulty tier. Lineups change, so this is config, not code.
_meta.verified_rule: verified: true means the model name was checked against that provider's own list. Everything else is marked and shown to the user as unchecked.
_meta.sources: OpenAI: developers.openai.com/api/docs/models and /models/all — Astra is described there as the flagship for complex reasoning and coding, Sol as the intelligence/cost balance, Luna for cost-sensitive high-volume work; gpt-6-astra has its own model page. Google: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog — gemini-4-argon reached GA on 13 Oct 2026 — plus the models page for the Flash and Flash-Lite ids. Anthropic: the Claude 5 family (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.5).
_meta.what_a_tier_means: Tiers are ENERGY classes, not marketing names, and each points at a different e_out range in config/sources.json. Providers do not publish active parameter counts for closed models, so placing a product in an energy class is our inference rather than a vendor statement. That is why every figure derived from it is a range.
_meta.recheck_before_the_demo: Names move every few weeks. Two things to re-read on the morning: GPT-6 Astra was still rolling out through OpenAI's Trusted Access Program, so it may not be callable on every account, and the model-retrieve reference page shows a shutdown_date of 2026-10-23 which looks like sample data rather than a real retirement for a six-week-old flagship. Confirm both. A judge who uses these tools daily will spot a dead model name faster than anything else on screen.
_meta.rule: The product never switches models. These only drive a suggestion the user accepts or ignores.
_meta.grok_status: Added from third-party sources that disagree on the newest model. Every Grok name is unverified; check xAI's /models endpoint before quoting one.

tiers.label: Small
tiers.description: Classification, extraction, translation, reformatting, grammar fixes.

tiers.label: Medium
tiers.description: Summaries, drafting, straightforward questions, light code.

tiers.label: Large
tiers.description: Hard reasoning, long multi-step work, architecture, debugging across many files, proofs.

small.note: Fast tier for lookups, renames and simple rewrites.

large.note: Hard reasoning and multi-file debugging. Effort levels reported for Opus 5: low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Some guides suggest xhigh for coding; check the official release page.

small.note: Cost-focused tier, listed on the Gemini API models page. Thinking level is set with thinking_level.

medium.note: Stable Flash model. Replaces gemini-3-flash, which is no longer in the lineup.

large.note: Flagship reasoning model, generally available 13 Oct 2026. Replaces gemini-3.1-pro. Confirm the thinking_level values for this model before quoting the effort.

small.note: OpenAI's docs point here for cost-sensitive, high-volume work, and name it as the replacement for the GPT-4 models retiring in January 2027.

medium.note: Described in OpenAI's docs as the balance of intelligence and cost. A GPT-6.1 Sol point release also exists; check which your plan exposes.

large.note: Flagship for complex reasoning and coding, with its own model page. Was still rolling out via the Trusted Access Program, so it may not be callable on every account yet.

small.note: Cheapest tier per OpenRouter and two aggregators; 2M context. Exact API id not confirmed.

medium.note: Low-cost tier in one 2026 guide; API release Apr 2026. Exact API id not confirmed.

large.note: Newest release named by several guides, but Grok 4.7 is also reported and is disputed. Confirm on xAI's /models endpoint.

default_assumed_tier_note: What we assume the user is on when they have not told us. Assuming large makes the suggestion look better, so the UI states this assumption out loud and lets the user change it.
